title: POC SLO measurement roadmap - Ravenswood kickoff
summary: Kickoff scoping for POC to define latency SLOs and measurement plan. Primary decision points: pick TTFT vs TPOT mix for acceptance, agree p95/p99 targets for two traffic profiles (interactive chat & batch summarization), confirm sampling approach (synthetic + production shadowing), and schedule benchmark runs. Next steps: Redwood to share benchmarking harness and initial run results; Ravenswood to provide traffic traces and dataset samples; follow-up benchmark run next week.
topics: p95/p99 target definition for interactive and batch
measurement methodology (warm vs cold, synthetic vs production samples)
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share benchmark harness repo and runbook by 2026-04-29
Leah Chen: Provide 7-day sampled traffic traces + 1000 anonymized messages by 2026-04-30
Priya Menon: Draft proposed telemetry schema and sampling queries (p50/p95/p99, tail-latency buckets) by 2026-04-29
Marco Diaz: Confirm compliance requirements for data used in benchmarks (PII scrub) by 2026-04-28
Samir Gupta: Run initial synthetic benchmark with 3 payload sizes and share CSV results by 2026-04-30

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-27 16:00 PDT | Duration 52m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood Solutions Eng); Evelyn Park (Ravenswood CTO), Marco Diaz (Ravenswood SRE), Leah Chen (Ravenswood PM), Tom Reynolds (Data Eng)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on SLOs for POC: TTFT vs TPOT, percentile targets, measurement plan and timelines.

00:00 Jordan: Okay everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, we're excited to kick off the POC with Ravenswood. Quick roll call?
00:08 Evelyn: Evelyn here, hi.
00:10 Marco: Marco.
00:12 Leah: Leah here.
:15 Samir: Samir from Redwood.
00:18 Jordan: Cool, I'll hand it to Priya to frame the technical approach then we'll get into success criteria.
00:25 Priya: Yeah thanks Jordan. So goal for today is pretty practical, um we want to define the latency SLOs in a way that maps to Raven--Ravenswood's apps. There's usually two dimensions we recommend: TTFT, time-to-first-token, and TPOT which some folks call time-per-token. We'll go through tradeoffs and propose p95/p99 targets for two traffic profiles: interactive chat (short context, low payload) and batch summarization (longer payloads).
00:52 Leah: Quick Q before you go on — when you say TPOT is that measured per token emitted or per input token? We had mixed definitions internally.
00:59 Priya: Great callout. For us TPOT is output token latency, so it's the average incremental time for each emitted token after first. So TTFT covers initial latency, TPOT captures throughput.
01:14 Marco: And for our SRE team we care about p99 tail spikes because clinical workflows can't have long tails. So we want p99 targets tight.
01:25 Priya: Understood. We typically propose an acceptance matrix: TTFT p95 for interactive channels, TTFT p99 as a softer gate, and TPOT p95 (and optionally p99) for long-running batch.
01:38 Evelyn: What's a ballpark numbers you usually see? Our current in-house on-prem has TTFT around 350-400ms for short prompts, but it's pretty variable.
01:49 Priya: Ok ballpark — on a dedicated GPU pool with optimized runtime, for 512-context chat we often hit TTFT p95 of 150-300ms depending on model size and quantization. TPOT for streaming small outputs can be 10-20ms/token p95 on well-batched workloads; for single-shot batch you may see higher. Those numbers vary with payload, batching, KV cache warm state, and whether there's compilation overhead.
02:20 Jordan: Worth noting customers often trade slight TTFT progs to reduce cost by batching more. So acceptance matrix must reflect tradeoffs.
02:30 Leah: Right, our product goal is perceived snappiness for clinicians — first token is most important in chat triage. For batch nightly summarization, throughput and cost matter more.
02:42 Tom: Also our payload distribution: 70% short messages ~ <200 tokens, 25% mid 200-1k, 5% long >1k. We'll share traces.
02:53 Priya: Perfect — that's the kind of input we need. For measurement plan we recommend two parallel tracks: synthetic microbenchmarks (controlled payloads across sizes, warm/cold runs, varying batch sizes) and production shadowing/trace replay to validate real tail behavior.
03:12 Marco: For production shadowing, we can't send real PHI outside the VPC. If we do shadowing in our private deployment we need KMS integration and audit logs.
03:23 Samir: We can run the Redwood Private plane inside your VPC and use your KMS; for the POC we can also run in Dedicated in our region but scrub data first.
03:34 Marco: Ok scrubbed data for the benchmark is fine.
03:37 Leah: On acceptance matrix, can we sketch concrete thresholds? For chat TTFT p95 = 250ms, TTFT p99 = 600ms? Is that realistic?
03:47 Priya: 250ms p95 on larger models is aggressive but feasible on dedicated GPUs with prefix caching and small context. If model is open Llama-variant 7B quantized, maybe 200-300ms p95. For p99 600ms is reasonable as a hard gate; we'd expect some cold cache outliers.
04:07 Jordan: Maybe frame it as target vs commitment: target TTFT p95 250ms, commitment TTFT p99 <= 800ms. And for TPOT for chat set p95 <= 25ms/token, for batch summarization TPOT p95 <= 40ms/token.
04:25 Evelyn: That framing is helpful. We also need to define sample sizes and measurement windows. We don't want a 1-hour run to falsely pass.
04:33 Priya: Agreed. For percentiles we recommend at least 100k samples for p95 stability and 250k+ for p99 in noisy distributions, or run over multiple days. For the POC baseline we can do 100k sample minimum and then assess variance.
04:50 Marco: Is that total requests or per workload? We have different traffic mixes.
04:54 Priya: Per workload per profile — so 100k for interactive chat profile, 100k for batch. If you have low-volume profiles we can use replay across multiple windows.
05:05 Tom: How do you handle warm/cold cache? Our real traffic will have a warm KV hit for many conversational flows.
05:12 Samir: We'll run separate sets: cold-start runs (clean KV/cache), warm runs (pre-warm KV and run synthetic sequences to prime the cache), and mixed runs. We'll tag telemetry.
05:23 Leah: Telemetry — what fields do we need from our side?
05:26 Priya: Minimum: request_id, timestamp, payload_length_tokens, prompt_type label (chat|batch), model_variant, whether KV cache hit, batch_size, first_token_timestamp, last_token_timestamp, total_tokens_out, and internal routing tag (hosted|dedicated|private). We will provide a schema.
05:45 Marco: Also include trace id for correlating backend events.
05:47 Priya: Yes trace id. We'll provide JSON lines spec.
05:52 Jordan: Ok let's talk acceptance gates and fallback. If POC fails TTFT p95 but meets TPOT and costs are better, do we accept?
06:02 Evelyn: Clinicians will be sensitive to first response, so TTFT matters more. We could accept a slightly higher TTFT if UX experiments show it's ok, but at least first token should be under 500ms p95.
06:18 Priya: A pragmatic acceptance matrix: green = TTFT p95 <= 300ms and TPOT p95 within agreed bucket; amber = TTFT p95 between 300-500ms with remediation plan and rollback; red = TTFT p95 >500ms. For p99 set hard ceiling 1200ms.
06:36 Marco: How do you simulate burstiness? Our busiest workflows have 20x burst factor for 30s every hour.
06:43 Samir: We'll run burst traffic tests using your traffic trace scaling. Run steady-state and ramp + spike patterns. We'll also validate autoscaling settings and cold-start behavior.
06:55 Leah: For the model variants, we plan to test two families: smaller quantized 8-bit models and a medium 13B variant. Can you show typical deltas?
07:06 Priya: Expect bigger model TTFT increase and slightly higher TPOT — e.g., 13B might double TTFT vs 7B depending on kernel selection. But quantization can close gap significantly. We'll recommend quantization profiles and batching config per model.
07:22 Jordan: Important to call out cost tradeoffs too — we'll give cost-per-1M tokens estimates for each config.
07:28 Evelyn: We'll need that for procurement.
07:31 Priya: Measurement plan timeline: Day 0-2: ingest traffic traces and sanitize; Day 3-5: run synthetic microbenchmarks across payload sizes and record warm/cold; Day 6: run production shadowing inside private deployment or replay in dedicated with scrubbed data; Day 7: debrief and acceptance decision.
07:51 Marco: Tight but doable. Can we push production replay earlier if we supply traces before Day 0?
07:58 Jordan: Yes if traces arrive today we can compress timeline.
08:01 Leah: About telemetry sampling — we can't send full raw traces off-network. Would Redwood accept aggregated metrics pushed to your dashboard?
08:10 Samir: For private runs we can ingest full telemetry inside your VPC and share aggregated CSVs. For hosted runs we'll ask for scrubbed payloads.
08:20 Priya: Also we instrument for histogram buckets (0-50ms,50-100ms,100-200ms,200-500ms,500-1s,1-5s) so p95/p99 analysis is robust.
08:32 Evelyn: For acceptance we want to include quality guardrails: model output correctness. If throughput is great but hallucinations increase we won't accept.
08:41 Jordan: Agree — we'll pair SLO acceptance with quality checks. For POC we'll run a sample of prompts against golden answers; Redwood to provide an eval harness or we can accept your eval set.
08:54 Leah: We'll prepare 200 prompt/response pairs for quality evaluation.
08:58 Priya: Great. On instrumentation we will provide Grafana dashboards with p50/p95/p99 and error budget calculation; plus CSV exports for audit.
09:10 Marco: For the cron nightly batch we need runbook steps if SLO breaches. What auto-fallbacks do you suggest?
09:18 Samir: For Dedicated we can route to smaller cheaper model variant under load, or shift to burst capacity in another region; also we have model-tier fallback policies. We'll propose an automatic fallback to quantized 7B when p95 exceeds threshold.
09:32 Marco: Need to ensure behavior is deterministic — if fallback changes output quality we must flag to product.
09:38 Priya: We'll add output-quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
09:44 Evelyn: Ok those are the right controls.
09:47 Jordan: Anything else?
09:49 Leah: One more on sampling frequency: For p99 stability, do you recommend continuous measurement or batch windows?
09:55 Priya: Continuous telemetry is best; but for POC we can do daily 1-hour window sweeps plus continuous low-sample telemetry. We'll compute rolling percentiles with sliding windows to detect regressions.
10:08 Marco: And how do you handle measurement noise caused by infra neighbors in multi-tenant?
10:12 Priya: For Dedicated we isolate GPU pools; for hosted we attribute by tenant and compare to baseline noise. We'll also include run of isolation tests to quantify neighbor noise.
10:24 Jordan: Let's recap next steps and owners.
10:27 Jordan: Action items — Jordan share harness, Priya telemetry schema, Samir initial synthetic runs, Leah and Tom share traces and quality eval. We'll tentatively meet 2026-05-04 to review results.
10:41 Evelyn: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
10:44 Jordan: Thanks all. End.

Notes: transcript imperfect: some labels and acronyms transcribed as "T T F T" or "K V cache" in places. References: benchmark harness repo (link provided after call), telemetry schema doc (link), sample CSV results to be attached.
